$comment: Rule catalog — planning. Standard 27. The catalog defines rule identity and metadata; project-policy.yml defines applicability; the evaluator produces evidence. None of the three may redefine the others.

rules.title: The plan lives in artifacts/project-plan-breakdown/
rules.description: A project with active work has a decomposed plan on disk, one ordered file per top-level section.
rules.rationale: A plan that exists only in a conversation is unavailable to the next agent, which is the failure Standard 5 exists to prevent.
rules.remediation: If this project already has an implementation and has not been reconstructed, run the project-reconstruction skill first (Standard 44), then apply /plan-structure and /plan-handoff to the reconstructed plan. Otherwise run /plan-structure and /plan-handoff, writing each top-level section to its own file under artifacts/project-plan-breakdown/. This run has not established which of the two holds.

rules.title: One file per top-level plan section
rules.description: Each top-level plan section is its own ordered Markdown file, so sequence survives and sections can be edited independently.
rules.rationale: A single monolithic plan file makes concurrent work and partial completion impossible to represent.
rules.remediation: Split the plan into NN-<section>.md files under artifacts/project-plan-breakdown/.

rules.title: Plan items define observable completion criteria
rules.description: Every executable plan item states criteria that are observable and objectively pass or fail.
rules.rationale: An agent should never have to guess whether a task is finished.
rules.remediation: Add an Acceptance Criteria section stating an observable condition, not an intention.
rules.$assuranceNote: A document check establishes that the section is present, not that its contents are observable or objective. Presence is partial evidence for the requirement.

rules.title: Plan items state how completion is proven
rules.description: Every executable plan item names the exact command or check that proves it done.
rules.rationale: Agents must verify their own work rather than declaring success from code inspection.
rules.remediation: Add a Verification line naming a command or check someone can run.

rules.title: The plan carries handoff context
rules.description: The plan transfers reasoning, conventions, and gotchas, not only instructions.
rules.rationale: A fresh agent with repository access and no chat history must be able to continue.
rules.remediation: Run /plan-handoff over the breakdown, or reproduce its behaviour manually.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether context genuinely transfers is a human judgement. No mechanical check is claimed.

rules.title: Executable plan items carry the six required fields
rules.description: Status, Purpose, Deliverables, Acceptance Criteria, Verification, and Dependencies appear on every executable plan item.
rules.rationale: Without Status, Acceptance Criteria, and Verification an item cannot be reported on, finished, or proven finished.
rules.remediation: Add the missing fields to the plan item. Where a field genuinely does not apply, say so explicitly rather than omitting it.

rules.title: A completed plan item's deliverables exist
rules.description: A plan item marked COMPLETE names deliverables that are present in the repository.
rules.rationale: A plan claiming completion for work that left no artifact is the plainest form of false green, and it is mechanically detectable.
rules.remediation: Either produce the deliverable or correct the item's status. Do not delete the deliverable line.
